query: Does the single-neuron latent dynamical model outperform trial-averaged PSTH baselines in fitting spike data, and what is the distribution of this improvement across the neural population?

analyse_plan.Objective: To quantify whether the single-neuron model produced higher likelihood than the trial-averaged firing rate computed for each chosen side and stimulus difficulty by computing log(Lmodel/LPSTH) for each neuron across the two monkeys.
analyse_plan.Validation Checks: Verify that all likelihood comparisons are performed within the same two non-overlapping cross-validation splits D1 and D2 used for model selection. Confirm that the baseline PSTH predicts the instantaneous firing rate λ(t) on each trial using the trial-averaged firing-rate traces sorted by the chosen side and stimulus difficulty, computed in a 75-ms window sliding in 10-ms steps on D1 and evaluated on D2, and vice versa. Check that the PSTH likelihood for the observed spike times {t1, …, tN} in the interval [t0, tE] is computed as the standard likelihood of an inhomogeneous Poisson process, LPSTH = exp(-∫λ(t)dt)∏i λ(ti), with the integral evaluated using the trapezoidal rule. Verify that, unlike PSTH, the full model likelihood is a joint probability density of the observed spikes and a latent trajectory reaching a decision boundary for the first time at the trial end time tE, marginalized over all possible latent trajectories. Confirm that the model likelihood used for comparison is the normalized spike-only likelihood Lmodel = L[Y(t)|θ] / LtE, where LtE is the likelihood of the latent trajectory reaching a boundary for the first time at time tE. Check that the reported ratio is log(Lmodel/LPSTH), and that the distribution across neurons is tested with a Wilcoxon signed-rank test separately for monkey T and monkey O.
analyse_plan.Steps: 1. Load Data: Load spike times for each neuron, the chosen-side and stimulus-difficulty labels for each trial, and the two non-overlapping cross-validation splits D1 and D2 used for model selection. 2. Split Data for Cross-validation: Use the same two non-overlapping data splits D1 and D2 as used for model selection. 3. Compute the PSTH Baseline: Compute the trial-averaged firing rates for the left and right choice trials in a 75-ms window sliding in 10-ms steps on D1, sorted by the chosen side and stimulus difficulty, and use them as a prediction of the instantaneous firing rates for the left and right choice trials on D2, and vice versa. 4. Compute PSTH Likelihood: For the observed spike times {t1, …, tN} of a single neuron during the time interval [t0, tE] on each trial, compute the PSTH likelihood as the standard likelihood of an inhomogeneous Poisson process, LPSTH = exp(-∫λ(t)dt)∏i λ(ti), where λ(t) is the PSTH for each chosen side and stimulus difficulty; compute the time integral using the trapezoidal rule. 5. Compute Full Model Likelihood: Evaluate the full single-neuron model likelihood for each validation trial as the joint probability density of the observed spikes and a latent trajectory reaching a decision boundary for the first time at the trial end time tE, marginalized over all possible latent trajectories. 6. Normalize the Model Likelihood: Compute the spike-only model likelihood as Lmodel = L[Y(t)|θ] / LtE, where LtE is the likelihood of the latent trajectory reaching a boundary for the first time at time tE; compute LtE analogously to the full model likelihood, but using only {t0, tE} observations and evolving the latent probability density with the Fokker–Planck equation without the probability decay term due to spike emissions. 7. Calculate the Likelihood Ratio: Compute log(Lmodel/LPSTH) for each neuron and average the value over the two cross-validation splits. 8. Statistical Test: Test whether the distribution of log(Lmodel/LPSTH) across neurons is greater than the PSTH baseline using the reported Wilcoxon signed-rank test separately for monkey T and monkey O. 9. Save Key Results: Save the cross-validated LPSTH values, normalized Lmodel values, log(Lmodel/LPSTH) for each neuron, the neuron identities, and the monkey labels used for the panel. 10. Visualization: Generate boxplots showing the distribution of log(Lmodel/LPSTH) across neurons for monkey T and monkey O.

key_analysis_results: Our model produced significantly higher likelihood than the trial-averaged firing rate computed for each chosen side and stimulus difficulty (log(Lmodel/LPSTH), median (Q1–Q3) 21.2 (7.27–48.5), P < 10^-10, n = 117 for monkey T; 9.39 (1.73–25.6), P = 1.3 × 10^-6, n = 67 for monkey O, Wilcoxon signed-rank test).
key_analysis_conclusions: This result indicates that single-trial firing rates deviate considerably from their trial average, and our model successfully captured this variation.

summary_report.abstract: The single-neuron model produced significantly higher likelihood than the trial-averaged firing rate computed for each chosen side and stimulus difficulty, indicating that the latent dynamical model captured single-trial variation beyond the PSTH baseline.
summary_report.methods: Model performance was evaluated within the same two non-overlapping cross-validation splits D1 and D2 used for model selection. The PSTH baseline predicted the instantaneous firing rate λ(t) on each trial using the trial-averaged firing-rate traces sorted by the chosen side and stimulus difficulty, computed in a 75-ms window sliding in 10-ms steps on D1 and evaluated on D2, and vice versa. For the observed spike times {t1, …, tN} of a single neuron during the time interval [t0, tE] on each trial, the PSTH likelihood was computed as the standard likelihood of an inhomogeneous Poisson process, LPSTH = exp(-∫λ(t)dt)∏i λ(ti), with the integral evaluated using the trapezoidal rule. Unlike PSTH, the full model likelihood on each trial is a joint probability density of the observed spikes and a latent trajectory reaching a decision boundary for the first time at the trial end time tE, marginalized over all possible latent trajectories. Therefore, for comparison with PSTH, the model likelihood used in Fig. 3a was the normalized spike-only likelihood Lmodel = L[Y(t)|θ] / LtE, where LtE is the likelihood of the latent trajectory reaching a boundary for the first time at time tE. The reported quantity in the panel is log(Lmodel/LPSTH), tested across neurons with a Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
summary_report.results: The single-neuron model produced significantly higher likelihood than the trial-averaged firing rate computed for each chosen side and stimulus difficulty. Specifically, log(Lmodel/LPSTH) had a median (Q1–Q3) of 21.2 (7.27–48.5) for monkey T (P < 10^-10, n = 117) and 9.39 (1.73–25.6) for monkey O (P = 1.3 × 10^-6, n = 67), showing that the model outperformed the PSTH baseline across neurons in both monkeys.
summary_report.discussion: This result indicates that single-trial firing rates deviate considerably from their trial average, and our model successfully captured this variation. Because the comparison uses the spike-only model likelihood normalized by the probability of the reaction time, the reported ratio specifically reflects how well the model explains the observed spike times relative to the PSTH baseline.
